> [!Note]
> [v25.07r5738](https://github.com/zufuliu/notepad4/releases/tag/v25.07r5738) and later no longer supports Windows XP, Windows Server 2003 (see issue #974) and Windows 8/8.1 on ARM32 (Windows RT) (see issue #1023), use [v25.06r5696](https://github.com/zufuliu/notepad4/releases/tag/v25.06r5696) instead.

## Changes Since [v26.08r6282](https://github.com/zufuliu/notepad4/releases/tag/v26.08r6282)
* Scintilla updated to 5.6.7, see https://www.scintilla.org/ScintillaHistory.html for the changes.
* Add menu "File -> Update File Time" to touch current file (update modification time without change attribute or content), issue #1310. d5a47e02e613afff63323d5cc577590d1089fc11
* Improved Russian translation, contributed by @Dimmitrius in PR #1308. 752defc886b53cd813b8a1c95bf21f49aa49ffbc
* Use short name for manually saved backup file, issue #1314. 26ca81ad6f844bcb6cbd785606f24cb919a2f5f6
* Lexer and API updates: HTML and PHP (91959ac6d1db696c0b45c6bc647cccb8081341a1, 4336a7824c608b019b2691a8b7170203e430880a, 3edbb3217d013ef5532fa2f615181bf3deb3baed, f72a811afd4d03b71c2801cd17491295d5d51f40, 2c69a0528837c90eef1a24bc3a76573afdcfcdda, a68c27d2f3c121a2bc799093c6b080fa10e32fad, etc.), Perl (1d06d41be25a9df959aa3897b90cd5e787f8755b), Python (046570920ce9067ef581473601dc20abe4fa5567), SQL (71c417502987ed17f323a7198571c05498d786ef, 537c435ba5c85604098657f8c9396c8b3b3bdd4d), WebAssembly (b5a5108259cdb9206b4fb2db01ccf4c438ab066c, 495b835a3c622146f12aac761c1ed2b2963b2cb7), XML (d851dbeaa52bb146cf28f1d07666fbd839c49474).
* Fix multiple "Inconsistent Line Endings" dialogs after file auto reloading, issue #1317. bc6c799223dadbaeabfc9f8125a6545cb162d64b
* Other bug fixes and improvements.

## Behavior Changes
* `/g line[,column]` (same as `-g line[,column]`) command line switch is changed to case sensitive (contributed by @lifenjoiner in PR #1305, 7522f0b8782aac168bc652b1701dbf04680fd898):
  * `/G line[,column[,tabwidth]]`: treat tab character as variable columns up to tab width (i.e. tab expansion), other character as single column. when `tabwidth` is zero or omitted use default document tab width.
  * `/g line[,column[,type]]`: no tab expansion, treat each character (when `type` is zero or omitted) or byte (when `type` is one) as single column. This matches Visual Studio and many others application where column is just character without tab expansion.
  * When `column` is negative: no tab expansion, treat each character as single column. negative column on "Goto" dialog is treated the same.
* Style configuration for JavaScript inside HTML is moved into standalone JavaScript scheme (same as PHP). dfa772f6d492157dec0247cda353ab4828cfff70

1. [Platform Update for Windows 7](https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/download/details.aspx?id=36805) is required for AVX2 version to use Direct2D on Windows 7 and Server 2008 R2.

wox.changelog:
Plugins can now open native windows and let you interact directly with search previews. Timer and Dictation are now standalone plugins you can install from the Wox Store as needed. We explain the move in [Keeping Wox Simple](https://www.woxlauncher.com/blog/a-smaller-core-with-plugins.html).

![Wox v2.5.0 Native UI for Plugins cover with an illustrated chart preview](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Wox-launcher/Wox/refs/heads/master/screenshots/changelog-v2.5.0-woxview.png)

- Add
  - [`WoxView`] Fill out forms, change options, and explore live charts in plugins that use WoxView, either in a separate window or right from a search result.
  - [`Snippets`] Save and search text you use often. Copy a snippet from Wox or set it to expand when you type a keyword. Snippets can insert values such as today's date or the current clipboard text. [#4702](https://github.com/Wox-launcher/Wox/issues/4702)

- Improve
  - [`Timer` and `Dictation`] Install either plugin from the Wox Store when you need it. Wox carries over your existing plugin settings when you upgrade.
  - [`Screenshot`] Highlight parts of a screenshot and edit the strokes later. Choose a preset aspect ratio and keep it locked as you resize the capture area. [#4704](https://github.com/Wox-launcher/Wox/issues/4704)
  - [`AI Chat`] Connect to local models through LM Studio and see an indicator while waiting for a reply. [#4692](https://github.com/Wox-launcher/Wox/issues/4692)
  - [`Quick Jump`] Type to search in Directory Opus, with the search box appearing next to the active pane. [#4688](https://github.com/Wox-launcher/Wox/pull/4688) [@momadacoding](https://github.com/momadacoding)
  - [`Converter`] Convert Unix timestamps to your local date and time with `to datetime` or `to dt`. [#4685](https://github.com/Wox-launcher/Wox/issues/4685)
  - [`Hotkey`] Use Insert or Delete as a shortcut on its own, and trigger shortcuts by holding supported keys on Windows, macOS, and Hyprland.
  - [`Query`] Search within filter options and save default selections for each plugin command.
  - [`Plugin`] See installation and update progress in the toolbar, and take action directly from plugin notifications.
  - [`Plugin Store`] See download and star counts, and sort by downloads, stars, name, or recent updates.

- Fix
  - [`Clipboard`] Read the latest clipboard contents on Wayland and preserve text without appending a newline.
  - [`Notes`] Preserve blank lines when switching between Markdown and preview, and keep headings from being clipped.
  - [`Settings`] Keep the active field focused and preserve its selection when plugin settings refresh after saving.
  - [`Quick Jump`] Keep File Explorer context menu shortcuts working when type-to-search is enabled. [#4698](https://github.com/Wox-launcher/Wox/pull/4698) [@yiumanlenong](https://github.com/yiumanlenong)

- Store
  - Plugin
    - [Timer](https://github.com/Wox-launcher/Wox.Plugin.Timer) Create and manage countdown timers [@Wox-launcher](https://github.com/Wox-launcher)
    - [Dictation](https://github.com/Wox-launcher/Wox.Plugin.Dictation) Offline speech recognition with AI refinement and custom actions. [@Wox-launcher](https://github.com/Wox-launcher)
    - [MultiTranslate for Wox](https://github.com/designstudio/MultiTranslate-for-Wox) Multi-provider translation for Wox. Google, Microsoft, DeepL and more. UI follows the Wox language automatically. [#4694](https://github.com/Wox-launcher/Wox/pull/4694) [@designstudio](https://github.com/designstudio)
    - [SiYuan](https://gist.github.com/hsopex/64693eab1cf4e4e62fa200faae087976) Search SiYuan notes and quickly create flash notes [#4699](https://github.com/Wox-launcher/Wox/pull/4699) [@hsopex](https://github.com/hsopex)

copytranslator.changelog:
### 主要更新（含使用方式）

#### 🚀 翻译能力增强

- 新增阿里云、Azure、DeepL、腾讯云、腾讯交互、Yandex、火山翻译引擎
- 新增彩云翻译与 Bing 词典引擎
- 支持 NVIDIA NIM 与 OpenRouter 自定义翻译器模板
- Google 翻译整合多后端（官方/Simply/Lingva），并优化 API 模式性能
- Lingva/Simply 增加响应校验与重试机制
- 更新谷歌翻译 API 镜像地址与超时时间

**如何使用：**
- 设置 → 翻译器管理：启用新增引擎或词典，必要时填写对应配置
- 设置 → API 设置：在“AI 翻译供应商/自定义翻译器”中添加 NVIDIA NIM、OpenRouter 模板并保存
- 引擎列表：选择新增引擎即可开始翻译

#### 🧩 翻译器管理与配置

- 翻译器管理界面重构为表格布局，交互更清晰
- 新增分组配置（缓存/对比/双击），支持拖拽排序
- 配置校验细化，显示可保存/可启用状态
- 配置字段支持元数据渲染与下拉选项
- 各翻译引擎增加配置指南链接
- 默认翻译器改为百度

**如何使用：**
- 设置 → 翻译器管理：进入分组配置页进行拖拽排序
- 看到配置状态提示时，先保存再启用对应引擎
- 点击“配置指南”快速跳转到对应官方文档

#### 🎨 界面与体验优化

- 新增内容区域内边距与行高配置
- 操作项支持布局分组与响应式样式
- 新增 OCR 开关与配置页面（百度 OCR/PP-OCR）
- 新增“**不再显示使用技巧**”选项
- 增加便携模式支持，可在可执行目录旁加载配置

**如何使用：**
- 设置 → 外观：调整内容内边距与行高
- 设置 → OCR：开启 OCR 并选择供应商
- 设置 → 开关：关闭“使用技巧”提示
- 将配置放在可执行文件同目录的 copytranslator 文件夹中启用便携模式

#### 🌐 网络与系统能力

- 新增网络代理配置页面，支持 HTTP/SOCKS5
- 增加离线语言检测，提升识别速度与稳定性
- 修复代理开关动作配置错误

**如何使用：**
- 设置 → 网络代理：填写代理类型与地址
- 代理使用谷歌翻译的配置步骤见[常见问题](https://copytranslator.github.io/guide/questions.html#%E8%B0%B7%E6%AD%8C%E7%BF%BB%E8%AF%91%E9%80%80%E5%87%BA%E4%B8%AD%E5%9B%BD%E5%B8%82%E5%9C%BA%E7%9A%84%E8%A7%A3%E5%86%B3%E6%96%B9%E6%A1%88)

#### 📊 可观测性与文档

- 新增应用内事件匿名追踪，退出时保证统计数据刷新
- 更新翻译提示文案与图标资源
- 补充翻译实现机制技术文档与问题排查文档

altsnap.changelog:
## What's Changed

Allow to have **parameters for an action** #718, #749, For the mouse buttons it usually will not affect anyone. However for Keyboard shortcuts it changes completely the way they are configured. Fixes #711

You will have to click on the [+] button next to the keyboard shortcut drop list and configure the advanced action.

This generalise the Step Window Action to ie: `Step_U_32`, to Step Up of 32 pixels.

Action parameters are separated by underscore. It also applies to the command line options:
ie: `AltSnap.exe -afTransparency_S_128` will set the Transparency of the currently focused window to 128.

To see the list of possible parameters, look at the advanced configuration box for the keyboard shortcuts.
Those advanced actions can also be used as Mouse actions but you have to write them manually in the proper format.

* Unify Movement logic, #732, to prepare for #723.
* Send WM_SIZING during resize for grid-snapping apps (like putty) by @andrewachen in #723, #739
* Add `DragOutThresholdPx` in the `[Advanced]` section of the ini file. #737. Default is 20 pixels. The reason the option was added is because Windows 11 returns random erroneous values when querying the `SPI_GETMOUSEDRAGOUTTHRESHOLD` value.
* Proper per-monitor WindowListMenu dpi awareness. #748. Fixes #747
* Updated German translation by @Ichisich
* Updated Ukrainian translation by @acid-jack
* Updated French and Italian Translations.
* Updated Polish translation by @xeophyte
* Updated Japanese translation by @coolvitto

unigetui.changelog:
# Devolutions UniGetUI 2026.3.4

This release adds a docked package details panel, a Manager Health page, and two new extensions: Agent Skills, and Xcode on macOS. It also adds new options for updates, notifications and shutting down, and fixes many update, display and performance bugs.

### New Features
* Added a package details panel that can stay open beside the package list on the Installed, Discover and Updates pages. It follows the selected package. Open it from the footer, with Ctrl+Shift+D (Cmd+Shift+I on macOS), or from the right-click menu.
* Added a Manager Health page that shows when each package manager last worked or failed, with repair actions. Each package manager also has a setup guide, linked from its status card when the tool isn't found.
* Added an Agent Skills extension for finding, installing and updating skills and plugins for Claude Code, Codex, GitHub Copilot and Cursor. It is off by default, under Settings > Extensions.
* Added an Xcode extension on macOS 13 and later. It downloads, installs, updates and switches between several Xcode versions, and manages Simulator runtimes, after you sign in with your Apple ID. It is off by default, under Settings > Extensions.
* Git Repositories now shows the size of each clone and worktree, and handles refresh failures more clearly.
* When a UniGetUI update is ready, you can now read its release notes before installing it, then update now, update when you quit, or skip that version. Open it from the update notification or from **More > Check for UniGetUI updates**. Quitting UniGetUI no longer installs a waiting update unless you choose to.
* Added an option to install UniGetUI updates automatically while it runs in the background with nothing else in progress (Windows, off by default).
* New per-package installation options:
  * **Skip major updates**, to keep getting minor and patch releases without moving to the next major version.
  * **Uninstall, then reinstall when updated**, for packages that only update cleanly from scratch.
* Added **Shut down when finished** to the operations panel menu (Windows). It shuts the computer down after the current operations, with a 60-second countdown you can cancel.
* Added an option to quit UniGetUI when automatic updates find nothing to install.
* Added an option to keep update notifications on screen until you dismiss them (Windows).
* Package lists can now scroll horizontally instead of squeezing columns. Turn off **Fit columns to the window** in the column menu.

### Improvements
* Downloaded installers are now checked against their published hash, and the installer's signer is shown.
* .NET Tool now uses the feeds in your NuGet configuration, including private feeds, and detects updates on Artifactory feeds.
* Improvements to WinGet searches.
* WinGet now lists updates that it can only apply by reinstalling, for example when a new version switches installer type.
* At startup, update checks now wait for each package manager's installed list, which reduces the load on machines with many packages.
* Pip no longer uses or updates Python environments that belong to other apps.
* Grid and icon cards on Software Updates now show the new version.
* Indeterminate progress bars use much less GPU on Windows.
* Screen readers now announce the tab names in installation options and operation history.

### Bug Fixes
* Fixed a restart staying pending forever after rebooting.
* Fixed WinGet offering an update when another installed copy of the app was already newer.
* Fixed Steam and other launcher games being listed as WinGet packages with a permanent update.
* Fixed WinGet portable apps losing their command links when updated without administrator rights.
* Fixed an empty Discover search returning nothing on some private WinGet repositories.
* Fixed the installer-host warning showing again on every update of some packages.
* Fixed scheduled update checks installing updates at startup.
* Fixed the operation history file growing to hundreds of MB and using gigabytes of memory.
* Fixed UniGetUI repeatedly offering a self-update it couldn't install on Linux `.deb` and `.rpm` installs.
* Fixed the window frame, shadow and corners when Windows 11's rounded corners are turned off, and centered the Close button.

Thank you to everyone who reported issues and contributed improvements to the project.

**Full Changelog:** https://github.com/Devolutions/UniGetUI/compare/v2026.3.3...v2026.3.4

mpv.changelog:
We are excited to announce the release of mpv 0.42.0.

Key highlights:

* libcurl based network backend with HTTP/2, HTTP/3 and connection reuse
* DVD-Video, Blu-ray HDMV and BD-J menu navigation
* DVD-Audio playback
* Direct playback of .iso images of DVD-Video, DVD-Audio and Blu-ray discs
* Dolby Vision Profile 7 enhancement layer support in `gpu-next`
* MPEG-TS programs and HLS variants are exposed as editions
* DSD-over-PCM (DoP) passthrough with `--audio-spdif=dsd`
* Support for SRV3 (YouTube) subtitles via subrandr library
* Context menu populated from the new `menu.conf`, bound to right click
* `floating` OSC layout with Fluent icons (`--script-opts=osc-layout=floating`)
* API that allows integration between the OSC and (third-party) thumbnailer scripts
* Wayland session management
* Wayland color management through the protocol instead of the Vulkan API
* scRGB output with `--target-trc=scrgb`
* Improved HDR colorspace signalling on DRM (Linux)
* D3D11 render API backend for libmpv
* Reworked terminal video outputs (`sixel`, `kitty` and `tct`)
* AMD Frame Rate Conversion filter (`--vf=amf_frc`)
* Rewritten display-sync audio drift compensation
* `--tls-verify` is enabled by default

This release requires FFmpeg 6.1 or newer and libplacebo 7.387.0 or newer.

Note that the release binary assets are our [CI builds](https://github.com/mpv-player/mpv/actions/runs/41936479105). These builds are reasonably useful. The Windows _full_ builds (`*-w64-mingw32-full.zip`) are bigger and aim to provide the complete experience.

# Features

## New

- sub: add subrandr renderer support

trilium.changelog:
# v0.107.0
> [!NOTE]
> If you enjoyed this release, consider showing a token of appreciation by:
> 
> *   Pressing the “Star” button on [GitHub](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium) (top-right).
> *   Considering a one-time or recurrent donation to the [lead developer](https://github.com/eliandoran) via [GitHub Sponsors](https://github.com/sponsors/eliandoran) or [PayPal](https://paypal.me/eliandoran).

> [!TIP]
> For Linux users: Trilium is now available on [Flathub](https://flathub.org/en/apps/org.triliumnotes.Trilium)!

This is the release where a text note stops being a single document. Notes can be embedded, quoted and referenced inside other notes and edited where they appear, laid out in columns and tabs, and mixed with drawings, attached files and video. Tables in text notes get the tools they had been missing, from merged cells to sorting, and the old layout is gone, a year after the new one replaced it.

Around the editor, the parts of the app that everyone touches were rebuilt: the context menus and the note autocomplete, the full search and the jump dialog, the launch bar and the tree. Shared pages look like the app again and render collections with their own views, and the calendar and geo map collections get the properties dialogs the board already had.

The AI integration becomes something to trust with a real database: every tool call asks before it reads or changes a note, a ChatGPT Codex subscription can stand in for an API key, and local models get web search through a search engine of your choice. On phones, iOS has a new layout and both apps navigate without a sidebar.

## 💡 Key highlights

### The text editor became a block editor

A text note used to be a document: one body of rich text, with other notes reachable only through links. It is now a composition. A note can embed another note and let you edit it where it sits, quote a few of its blocks and keep the quote current, or point at one paragraph of it instead of at the whole note.

*   [Editable transclusion](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/11926): an included text or code note is edited inside the host note with the full editor, and one undo history covers both.
*   [Live excerpts](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/11925) quote blocks of another note. They stay in sync, and an edit made in the excerpt is saved back to the source.
*   [Block references](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/12069) link to a paragraph, heading, table or range of blocks. The target opens scrolled to the block and highlighted, and on a shared page every block has a public link of its own.

Layout caught up with content. [Multicolumn layouts](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/11958) put two to four columns side by side and stack them on narrow screens. [Drawing canvases](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/11829) are sketched in place with Excalidraw and saved with the note. Files are [attached](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/11795) in one step, as inline embeds for PDFs and spreadsheets or as links, and YouTube videos and web audio or video play inside the note. A block handle moves blocks, images and tables, a "+" on an empty line opens the slash commands, and one [link dialog](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/12358) serves web links, note links and anchors from a popover at the cursor.

The include box itself was [reworked](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/11798): a compact title row with a caption, fullscreen, a link from the embed to its note and back, Markdown included as source, split or preview, code with folding and line numbers, and resizing by dragging a corner or an edge.

Contributed by @adoriandoran.

### Tables in text notes

Tables were the editor's weak spot: no merged cells, no sorting, and anything past a few rows meant switching to a spreadsheet note. The [table context menu](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/11774) now merges and unmerges cells, distributes columns, and inserts or deletes many rows and columns at once. A column sorts by its values, with dates, times, numbers and text detected and ordered per the note's language, and Alt+arrows move rows and columns while keeping merged cells and header rows intact.

Wide tables scroll sideways under a sticky header, and on touch screens a column bar resizes and selects columns while corner handles select cell ranges. The insert form takes any size up to 1000 × 100, with header rows and columns.

Contributed by @adoriandoran.

### AI that asks before it acts

Two things kept many users away from the AI integration: paying per token, and handing a model write access to their notes. Both change in this release.

ChatGPT Codex subscriptions, including the free plan, and OpenRouter join Claude Code, GitHub Copilot and Antigravity as providers, so an existing subscription can drive Trilium's chat. [Custom search engines](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/11878) (Brave Search, Tavily, Exa, Serper, Perplexity, or a self-hosted SearXNG) give web search to local models and to providers that have none of their own, such as DeepSeek.

[Before a tool runs](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/12116), the chat shows what the AI is about to read or change and waits for you to allow or deny it, for that call or for the rest of the conversation. The Tools menu sets the default: always ask, ask only before changes, or never ask. It works the same with API keys and with subscription providers.

### Shared pages look like the app

A note shared to the web rendered in a theme of its own, and a shared collection appeared as a plain list of its children. Shared pages now use a [theme built from the app's own look](https://github.com/TriliumNext/Trilium/pull/11979), in light and dark, and a shared board, table, calendar or other collection renders with the same view it has inside Trilium.

Drawings appear as theme-aware SVG pictures instead of a download link, and every bloc

drawio.changelog:
## Release Notes for 32.7.4

[Windows Installer](https://github.com/jgraph/drawio-desktop/releases/download/v32.7.4/draw.io-32.7.4-windows-installer.exe)
[Windows No Installer (zip)](https://github.com/jgraph/drawio-desktop/releases/download/v32.7.4/draw.io-32.7.4-windows.zip)
[macOS - Universal](https://github.com/jgraph/drawio-desktop/releases/download/v32.7.4/draw.io-universal-32.7.4.dmg)
Linux - [deb](https://github.com/jgraph/drawio-desktop/releases/download/v32.7.4/drawio-amd64-32.7.4.deb), [AppImage](https://github.com/jgraph/drawio-desktop/releases/download/v32.7.4/drawio-x86_64-32.7.4.AppImage) or [rpm](https://github.com/jgraph/drawio-desktop/releases/download/v32.7.4/drawio-x86_64-32.7.4.rpm)

**ChangeLog:**

- Uses electron 44.11.3
- Fixes HTML export from the command line failing or hanging on very large diagrams
- Stops reading a diagram embedded in a PNG or PDF file once it is longer than the longest text the app can hold, instead of decompressing all of it first
- Command line PDF exports with --width or --height now contain the diagram, fitted to that size, instead of an empty page [jgraph/drawio-desktop#2162]
- Command line PDF and SVG exports fill in %pagecount% [jgraph/drawio-desktop#2601]
- Command line exports no longer wait forever for an image whose server never answers: an image that makes no progress for 15 seconds is left out and the export completes
- Links in exported SVG and PDF files keep only safe link types, and PDF exports no longer contain links to the install folder
- The Grid option of the advanced export dialog now works in the desktop app
- Removes data sources from the desktop app, where they could never load
- The public repository now carries the Linux source of each release; the Windows and macOS packaging files are no longer published there
- Updates to [draw.io core 32.7.4](https://github.com/jgraph/drawio/blob/v32.7.4/ChangeLog). All changes from 32.6.10 to 32.7.4 are added in this build.

**Testing:**

Verified against the packaged, signed macOS build. Windows and Linux packages were verified from the produced release artifacts, their sizes and update manifests, rather than by running them.

Base checks

- Launch, open a file passed on the command line, add and edit shapes, change styles, undo and redo, copy and paste, save without a dialog, reopen, insert, rename and delete pages, and zoom
- Export to PNG, JPEG, SVG, PDF, XML and HTML from the command line, covering scale, border, transparency, cropping, page selection with -p and --size page, and to PNG and PDF from the app
- Diagram round trip in an exported PNG and PDF, including reopening the exported PDF and recovering both pages and their contents
- Mermaid and CSV import, and the --layout and --normalize options from the command line
- Shape search, stencils and shape bundles, the export dialogs and the print dialog
- Settings survive a restart
- The macOS bundle is signed with a Developer ID certificate under the hardened runtime, is notarised and stapled, and the Quick Look app extension is sandboxed, separately signed and registered
- The Electron security fuses are applied
- Reads, writes and file checks of paths the user has not authorised are refused, and file and javascript links are not opened externally
- The update manifests of all five platforms name this version and files that exist
- 348 unit tests pass

Command line exports

- %pagecount% resolves in PDF exports of all pages, of a single page and in SVG exports, and page variables work for files without pages [jgraph/drawio-desktop#2601]
- A 3000 by 97 shape exported with --width 500 gives a page 500 units wide that the diagram fills edge to edge, --height gives the requested height, and --width with all pages gives each page that width [jgraph/drawio-desktop#2162]
- With an image server that accepts the connection and never answers, PNG, PDF and SVG with embedded images complete in 16 to 18 seconds with the rest of the diagram
- HTML export of a PNG or PDF with an embedded diagram recovers all three pages, and a PNG without a diagram is reported and skipped in a folder export

Links in exports

- An SVG export keeps https and relative links and drops ms-msdt, vbscript, search-ms and data links; a PDF export keeps only the https link and no link to the install folder
- Links of a page used as a background are not active in PDF exports

Checks around the changes

- The Grid option changes PNG and PDF exports from the advanced export dialog
- Copy as Image places a PNG image on the system clipboard
- Data sources are absent from the menus and from Page Setup
- Starting with DRAWIO_ENV=dev loads the packaged editor without errors

Changelog for restic 0.20.0 (2026-11-19)
=======================================

The following sections list the changes in restic 0.20.0 relevant to restic users. The changes are ordered by importance.

Summary
-------

 * Sec [#22178](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/22178): Fix ownership when `restore --ownership-by-name` cannot resolve names
 * Sec [#22180](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/22180): Reject duplicate or out-of-order node names during `restore`
 * Fix [#21977](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21977): Don't crash on truncated key or config file
 * Fix [#22007](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/22007): Redact `swift` backend password in debug log output
 * Fix [#22051](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/22051): Reject empty repository location files
 * Fix [#22085](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/22085): Restore partially matching hard-linked files correctly
 * Fix [#22092](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/22092): Handle empty directories from older repaired snapshots
 * Fix [#22112](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/22112): Don't reset `stats` progress bar counters for every snapshot
 * Fix [#22120](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/22120): Improve error message when `prune` fails to list pack files
 * Fix [#22136](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/22136): Improve resilience of repository v2 upgrade rollback
 * Fix [#22163](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/22163): Error on too large numbers in `--keep-within*` durations
 * Fix [#22181](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/22181): Do not delete files in directories whose tree cannot be loaded
 * Chg [#22104](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/22104): Require Go 1.26.10 or newer
 * Enh [#3129](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/3129): Add JSON support to `prune` command
 * Enh [#5189](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/5189): Add option to disable AWS S3 dual-stack endpoints
 * Enh [#5248](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/5248): Add warmup support for `check` on the S3 backend
 * Enh [#5372](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/5372): Support specifying snapshot ID in `list packs` command
 * Enh [#5741](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/5741): Support Multi-Bucket Application Keys in the `b2` backend
 * Enh [#21845](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21845): Handle missing pack files in `repair packs`
 * Enh [#21870](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/21870): Show excluded items during `backup` in verbose mode
 * Enh [#21883](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21883): Handle corrupted pack files in `find --pack`
 * Enh [#21892](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/21892): Make `repair snapshots --forget` remove broken snapshots
 * Enh [#21937](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21937): Reduce memory usage of the in-memory index

Details
-------

 * Security #22178: Fix ownership when `restore --ownership-by-name` cannot resolve names

   When restoring with `--ownership-by-name`, user or group names that could not be resolved on the restore host (or were not recorded in the snapshot) caused restic to change the owner of the restored file to UID/GID 0. Combined with restored setuid/setgid bits this could produce unintentional setuid-root files.

   Restic now instead falls back to the numeric UID/GID stored in the snapshot and prints a warning when a name cannot be resolved.

    [#22178](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/22178) [#22185](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/22185) 

 * Security #22180: Reject duplicate or out-of-order node names during `restore`

   A tree containing a symlink and a directory with the same name could let `restore` write through the symlink to files outside the restore target.

   Restic now rejects trees whose node names are not strictly increasing during restore and reports an error instead of restoring such a snapshot.

   Thanks to Mario Ramos (@marrionesa), calif.io, Zachariah Mithani (AploSec) and Manuel Riel (@m3nu) for reporting this.

    [#22180](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/22180) [#22190](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/22190) 

 * Bugfix #21977: Don't crash on truncated key or config file

   Restic previously crashed with a slice bounds panic when the repository contained a key or config file that was shorter than the encryption overhead, for example after an upload was interrupted. Since every command has to read a key file, the whole repository became unusable until the file was removed.

   This has now been fixed, and restic instead reports that the file is too short.

    [#21977](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/21977) 

 * Bugfix #22007: Redact `swift` backend password in debug log output

   Restic could previously write the OpenStack Swift backend password in clear text to the debug log when debug logging was enabled. The password came from the environment variables `OS_PASSWORD` and `ST_KEY`. It is now redacted.

    [#22007](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/22007) 

 * Bugfix #22051: Reject empty repository location files

   Previously, if the `--repository-file` option or `RESTIC_REPOSITORY_FILE` environment variable referred to a file that was either empty or contained only whitespace, restic used the current directory for the repository.

   This has now been fixed, and restic instead reports an error in this case.

    [#22051](https://github.com/restic/restic/issues/22051) [#22052](https://github.com/restic/restic/pull/22052) 

 * Bugfix #22085: Restore partially matching hard-linked files correctly

   When restoring over an existing file which had hard links and was partially different from the file in the snapshot, restic used to replace the file with an empty one but only restored the changed parts. The restored file then contained zero bytes in the unchanged parts. Restic now instead rewrites the whole file in this case.

frp.changelog:
## Features

* frpc can verify server certificates using system CAs, optionally combined with CAs from `trustedCaFile`.
* `frpc reload` now refreshes certificate files for unchanged `https2http` and `https2https` proxies without interrupting existing connections. Failed refreshes keep the previous certificate and report the error in proxy status and logs while reload still succeeds.
* Added `metricsServer` to both frps and frpc, a separate listener for health checks, metrics and optional profiling that does not expose the dashboard or the admin API. It is disabled unless `metricsServer.port` is set, defaults to `127.0.0.1`, and has its own credentials and TLS. Setting the port serves `/metrics` on both: frps exposes runtime and business metrics, so `enablePrometheus` is not needed there, and frpc exposes Go runtime metrics only, without linking an extra metrics library.

  The `/healthz`, `/metrics` and pprof endpoints on `webServer`, `webServer.pprofEnable` and `enablePrometheus` still work but are deprecated: configure `metricsServer` instead. They will continue to work until v0.80.0 is released, and may be removed in v0.80.0 or later.

## Fixes

* Fixed proxy and visitor configuration changes being lost when reloading frpc during reconnection.
* Updated yamux to fix a 100% CPU busy loop after a session shuts down and a session close that could hang when the underlying connection (for example WebSocket) blocks on a write, which could also delay reconnection.
* frps now closes the multiplexed session of a replaced or failed control connection immediately, releasing its streams and work connections instead of keeping them until keepalive times out.
* Fixed a data race when frpc updates log prefixes while other goroutines are logging, which could crash the process.
* Fixed HTTPS and tcpmux route listeners leaving a pending connection open when the listener is removed during connection handoff; the connection is now closed instead of leaving the client to wait for a read timeout.

aria2-next.changelog:
## Summary

Aria2 Next 3.1.2 fixes downloads that could stay in the stopping state after a pause or removal, picks up its own unfinished files again when the same URL is added without `--continue`, and expands `${HOME}` in path options. Release assets cover the same seven platforms.

### Fixed

- A download whose disk write fails while it is being paused or removed now finishes stopping instead of waiting forever. Repeated stop requests no longer complete a task twice; a later request can only strengthen the outcome, so a removal wins over a pause and a pause over a requeue ([rayburst#832](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/rayburst/issues/832)).
- On Linux, `--file-allocation=falloc` and `prealloc` reserve space in 256 MiB steps, so pausing or removing a large download no longer waits for the whole file to be reserved ([rayburst#832](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/rayburst/issues/832)).
- Adding a URL again after its unfinished download was removed continues the file this engine left behind, even without `--continue`, when the server shows the same file: the same length, range support, and a matching strong ETag or Last-Modified. Otherwise the download gets a new numbered name as before, and a file that still belongs to a paused download is never taken over ([rayburst#842](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/rayburst/issues/842)).
- Path options such as `--dir`, `--save-session` and `--log` expand `${HOME}`, on the command line and in the configuration file, as aria2 does ([#94](https://github.com/AnInsomniacy/aria2-next/issues/94)).

### Changed

- A stop that takes longer than two seconds is logged with what it is waiting for, and a disk operation that takes longer than one second is logged at most once every ten seconds per file.

### Downloads

| --- | --- |
| Linux x86_64 | `aria2-next-3.1.2-linux-x86_64` |
| Linux ARM64 | `aria2-next-3.1.2-linux-aarch64` |
| macOS Apple Silicon | `aria2-next-3.1.2-macos-arm64` |
| macOS Intel | `aria2-next-3.1.2-macos-x86_64` |
| Windows x86_64 | `aria2-next-3.1.2-windows-x86_64.exe` |

system-informer.changelog:
# System Informer 4.0

The first 4.0 release: a new kernel/user transport, a Process Monitor, Hybrid Analysis integration, a JSON settings store, a rewritten installer, and a year of fixes across the app, driver, plugins, and phnt headers.

## Highlights

- Process Monitor (Tools menu): a driver-backed live log of process, thread, image, registry, file, handle and silo events with filtering, access-mask decoding, and configurable look-back.
- Hybrid Analysis integration (OnlineChecks): System Informer can now automatically check running processes and loaded images against Hybrid Analysis, showing verdicts directly in the process and module lists via a new Hybrid Analysis column. Unknown files can optionally be submitted for analysis. Results are cached locally so repeated lookups are free, and scanning is opt-in with per-service API keys, path exclusions, and rate handling built in.
- Ring-buffer informer transport in the kernel driver: large shared-memory ring instead of per-message port round-trips, with rate limiting and per-client statistics; informer callbacks run at APC/DPC level where possible.
- New installer: modern wizard with dark mode, DPI scaling, uninstaller, shortcut page, and atomic staged extraction with rollback — failed updates no longer leave a half-written directory.
- Updater: toast-notification flow with progress and actions; BITS, Delivery Optimization and Microsoft Store download back-ends.
- Low-latency mode (experimental, Windows 11): high-resolution provider timers.
- Per-monitor DPI and dark theme work throughout the app, plugins, and property sheets, including Windows 11 borders and much less resize flicker.

## Application

### New
- Users tab (logged-on sessions); process environment editor with multi-entry split editing; WMI tab gains MI support.
- Columns: Short user name, service Username, thread RPC usage, thread kernel stack, handle reference count/size, extended GDI/handle details, ALPC port state; GPU/NPU committed memory.
- Process tree: independent root/child sort options, Collapse/Expand All, aggregate-aware sorting; Ctrl-drag parent fix.
- Threads: Freeze/Thaw, suspended/wait-type highlighting; Modules: native/mapped highlighting and CLR metadata mapping.
- Memory strings search: parallel/bulk scanning, UTF-8, progress, sortable results.
- Services: multi-select start/pause with progress and retry; Run As: per-launch privilege selection and AppContainer launch.
- Handle protect/inherit changes without the driver; COM permission dialogs; desktop heap detection; UDP firewall-exempt port highlighting.
- System Information: reorderable sections, horizontal scrolling, per-CPU speed; overhauled tray mini-info window; energy statistics.
- Options: consolidated Highlighting page, per-tab layout persistence, advanced setting editor; settings.schema.json shipped for editors.
- Hold Shift at startup to launch the original Task Manager when System Informer is the replacement.

### Fixed
- I/O delta columns sorting by cumulative values; page/IO priority in Threads tab; protection column sort; username column not updating.
- Process affinity regressions (single and multi processor groups); main window stealing foreground at startup; previous-instance restore and handle leak.
- Hangs opening the security editor and AFD socket properties; crashes on CPUs without rdtscp, in snapshot handling, on "Current Power Scheme", and with WSL info when no distro is installed.
- Settings not saving on network shares; User Notes not reloaded on restart; Windows 7 import resolution.
- Numerous memory and handle leaks, out-of-bounds reads (CPU info, syscall list, AVX search), and dark-theme painting bugs.

## Kernel driver (KSystemInformer)

- Silo (container) informer; file informer now reports copy operations, access masks and image sizes; thread kernel-stack query; hash-result caching; dedicated system process for driver threads.
- Object protection reworked with broader handle-access stripping and on-demand protection; CID table population optimized; portable mode always unloads the driver on exit.
- Hardening: OBJ_DONT_REPARSE on all internal opens; message/dynamic-data validation and size math hardened; share-check/paging-file open options require MAXIMUM state; "securely created" state requires WinTcb/WinSystem creator; randomized minifilter altitude when load fails; rundown protection for hash/verify.
- Many correctness fixes: native-load race, ring-buffer signaling, informer state leak, file-op buffer/MDL handling, EPROCESS/VPB/pool-tag issues, image-mapping leak, registry post-op strings, thread handle guarantees.

## Security hardening (user mode)

- Updater: the downloaded installer is now re-verified from disk and held with a deny-write handle until launched, failing closed otherwise.
- phsvc: the elevated helper now pins the client image to Systchecks integrity before accepting connections.
- Overflow-checked size math in ACL/security-descriptor, heap and config parsing; DbgHelpVerifyMicrosoftChain setting to verify the dbghelp/symsrv signing chain; remote environment address validation.

## Hybrid Analysis & file reputation (OnlineChecks)

- Automatic reputation scanning of processes and modules with Hybrid Analysis; verdicts surface in a new Hybrid Analysis column and in the file properties.
- Optional automatic submission of unknown files to Hybrid Analysis for sandbox analysis.
- Opt-in setup flow with a Hybrid Analysis partner prompt; perd path exclusions so sensitive directories are never hashed orsubmitted; configurable startup delay.
- Batched hashing and requests with rate-limit handling, and a portable SQLite scan cache shared safely across multiple System Informer processes.

## Plugins

- ExtendedTools: ACPI tables, TPM boot log (WBCL), Power Grid/ and Startup Tasks dialogs; per-adapter/per-node GPU columns and GPU memory mini-info; disk rate columns; better firewall monitor.
- WindowExplorer:

sandboxie-plus.changelog: ![0 5 5](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/3890945/105014988-575cb680-5a41-11eb-90d5-d942d28184b2.png) ### Release Notes Sandboxie-Plus 1.19.1 introduces AI-assisted troubleshooting in SandMan. The new “Troubleshoot with an AI Agent” toolbar button lets you connect an MCP-compatible AI client to investigate a sandbox issue. The feature is off by default and uses a local named pipe with a one-time pairing code. SandMan shows you the exact configuration changes or commands the agent proposes and asks for approval each time. You can review the session history and choose whether to submit an issue report with the agent’s findings and a log of the actions taken. This release fixes two performance problems. Sandboxed applications that frequently look up localized strings or resources could suffer severe slowdowns, including frame rate drops in games. Those lookups now benefit from Windows’ cached language settings again. Sandboxie also removes a configuration locking bottleneck that forced concurrent process launches to wait on one another. Sandbox border labels can now appear on any of the four window edges. A dedicated Box Border tab lets you choose the font, position and text orientation. The built-in INI editors gain optional line numbers and Ctrl+G navigation, and the new CustomProcessCommandLine setting lets you conditionally add, remove or replace arguments when launching a sandboxed process. Version 1.19.1 also restores Windows 7 compatibility after a regression in 1.19.0 and fixes a hang when elevating sandboxed programs with Windows Administrator Protection enabled. Several SandMan crashes during startup, sandbox creation and shutdown have been fixed. The message log now has a size limit to prevent memory exhaustion during long sessions. For a full list of changes please review the [change log](https://github.com/sandboxie-plus/Sandboxie/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md#1191--5741---2026-10-21). #### You can support the project through donations, any help will be greatly appreciated. [](https://xanasoft.com/go.php?to=donate) #### If you have issues with an update installation, just uninstall the previous version keeping the sandboxie.ini and reinstall the new build.

zed.changelog:
This week's release includes reduced GPU usage across the app, a model picker for AI commit message generation in the Git Panel, a setting to hide the title bar, support for GPT-6.1 Terra, and faster scanning of large projects.

## Features

### AI

- Added support for GPT-6.1 Terra to the OpenAI provider. ([#66659](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66659); thanks [nymo](https://github.com/nymo))
- Added keyboard navigation to the agent thread switcher (opened with `ctrl-tab` from the Agent Panel or Threads Sidebar): `up` / `down`, `ctrl-n` / `ctrl-p`, and `home` / `end` move the selection, as do `ctrl-up` / `ctrl-down` while `ctrl` is still held. ([#66951](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66951); thanks [kinoute](https://github.com/kinoute))
- Added support for the Extra High thinking effort level for Gemini 4 Hydrogen (`gemini-4-hydrogen`), which now defaults to High. ([#67011](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/67011); thanks [LorenzoBiassio](https://github.com/LorenzoBiassio))
- Improved GitHub Copilot models to use their full context window when there is no long-context surcharge, and to display per-token pricing where available. ([#64302](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/64302); thanks [Jozef833](https://github.com/Jozef833))
- Improved memory usage when saving long agent threads. ([#66683](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66683); thanks [founderinaction](https://github.com/founderinaction))

### Git

- Added a model picker to the Git Panel's commit editor for choosing the model used for commit message generation. The choice is saved to the `agent.commit_message_model` setting. ([#50674](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/50674); thanks [soilSpoon](https://github.com/soilSpoon))

### Vim / Helix

- Added the `g r t` keybinding for `editor: go to type definition`, matching Neovim's default. ([#66759](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66759); thanks [ask4fusora](https://github.com/ask4fusora))
- Added the `] n` and `[ n` keybindings in visual mode for `vim: select next syntax node` and `vim: select previous syntax node`, matching Neovim's defaults. ([#66759](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66759); thanks [ask4fusora](https://github.com/ask4fusora))

### Languages

- Improved syntax highlighting of `#pragma` and `#undef` arguments in C and C++. ([#66875](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66875); thanks [imryanthedev](https://github.com/imryanthedev))

### Linux

- Improved ACP registry agent installation on musl-based Linux systems, such as Alpine, to use musl builds when available. ([#66914](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66914))

### macOS

- Updated the Git version bundled with Zed on macOS to 2.56.1. ([#67264](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/67264))

### Other

- Added a `title_bar.show` setting to hide the title bar always (`"never"`) or only in fullscreen (`"hide_in_full_screen"`). The default is `"always"`. ([#65671](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/65671); thanks [wuemeli](https://github.com/wuemeli), and thanks [xipeng-jin](https://github.com/xipeng-jin) for an earlier implementation in [#42540](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/42540))
- Added `editor: fold at current indentation level` to fold the whole document at the current line's indentation level. ([#66849](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66849))
- Added a `zed --debug-state` CLI flag that prints the running app's window, display, and platform state as JSON for debugging. ([#66852](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66852))
- Improved rendering efficiency to reduce GPU usage across the app, including when drawing paths (such as Git Graph lines), shadows, and content hidden behind other elements. ([#66806](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66806), [#66807](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66807), [#66809](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66809), [#66810](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66810), [#66811](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66811), [#66812](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66812))
- Improved battery life by animating spinners without re-rendering the views that contain them. ([#66896](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66896))
- Improved responsiveness during heavy filesystem activity, such as external builds creating or removing many files. ([#66835](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66835), [#66973](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66973), [#66990](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66990), [#67008](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/67008); thanks [RemcoSmitsDev](https://github.com/RemcoSmitsDev))
- Improved the time to scan large projects when they are opened. ([#67023](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/67023); thanks [ptweezy](https://github.com/ptweezy))
- Improved fuzzy matching performance when many candidates match. ([#66982](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66982); thanks [ptweezy](https://github.com/ptweezy))
- Improved performance of multibuffers with many files, such as large project search results. ([#67053](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/67053); thanks [ptweezy](https://github.com/ptweezy))
- Improved performance when large directories are removed or rescanned. ([#66962](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66962); thanks [ptweezy](https://github.com/ptweezy))
- Improved responsiveness of the completions menu with many matches. ([#66959](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/66959); thanks [ptweezy](https://github.com/ptweezy))
- Improved the onboarding page to keep the "Finish Setup" button visible while scrolling. ([#67079](https://github.com/zed-industries/zed/pull/67079); thanks [aakashbapna](https://github.com/aakashbapna))

escrcpy.changelog:
# 🚀 Escrcpy 3.3.1 — Unlock Existing Features, Embrace a New Chapter

Escrcpy 3.3.1 is a **transitional release** that bridges the gap between the existing version and the new billing and licensing system planned for Escrcpy 4.0.0 and later.

To ensure a smooth transition, **all existing features in Escrcpy 3.3.1 are available for free**, with no purchase, activation, or license verification required. This is a long-term policy for the existing version, not a limited-time promotion.

This release also improves the stability of embedded mirroring and application startup workflows.

## ✨ What's New

### 🔓 All Existing Features Unlocked

Due to adjustments to our billing platform and subscription system, all existing features in Escrcpy 3.3.1 are now available for free.

This policy is intended to help existing users transition smoothly to the new version strategy. You can continue using all features available in Escrcpy 3.3.1 without additional payment.

### 🖥️ Embedded Mirroring & Virtual Displays

- Introduced preliminary support for launching applications on virtual displays and using embedded mirroring.
- Improved the stability of application startup logic related to embedded mirrored virtual screens.
- Fixed abnormal mirroring control parameters when launching applications through shortcuts.
- Fixed an application launch issue affecting some Windows users.

### 🤖 Copilot Configuration

Copilot now requires users to configure a supported AI model provider, including the relevant API key, endpoint, and model settings.

If no provider is configured, the interface prompts users to complete the setup instead of automatically using the previous built-in service.

Please note that third-party AI model providers may charge for API usage according to their own pricing policies.

## ⚠️ Important Upgrade Notice

Due to adjustments to the billing and subscription system, users running Escrcpy 3.2.0 or earlier may encounter license verification issues or find that certain features no longer work correctly.

**We recommend upgrading to Escrcpy 3.3.1 as soon as possible.** All existing features in this release are unlocked and can be used without additional payment.

## 🔮 Looking Ahead: Escrcpy 4.0.0+

Escrcpy 4.0.0 and later versions are planned to introduce a new billing and licensing system, along with new features and services.

- **A new licensing system:** Future versions will use a separate licensing and purchasing system.
- **Launch promotion:** A three-day introductory promotion with special pricing is planned. Pricing and details will be announced separately.
- **Your existing version remains available:** You can continue using Escrcpy 3.3.1 and all its unlocked features without purchasing a newer version.
- **Previous purchases will not automatically transfer:** Purchases made under the previous system will not automatically grant paid entitlements under the new system.

Escrcpy 3.3.1 serves as a bridge between the existing version and the upcoming licensing system. You can continue using the current version or consider upgrading when the new version becomes available.

## 🙏 Thank You

Thank you for your continued support and feedback. We hope Escrcpy 3.3.1 provides a more stable experience and helps make this transition smooth as we prepare for the next chapter of Escrcpy.

stability-matrix.changelog:
## v2.17.0
> Full technical notes for this release: [docs.lykos.ai/stability-matrix/release-notes/2.17.0](https://docs.lykos.ai/stability-matrix/release-notes/2.17.0)
### Security
- Package installs now check HTTPS certificates against your operating system's certificate store instead of uv's built-in list, so certificates your OS has revoked are rejected. To opt out, set `UV_SYSTEM_CERTS` to `0` in Settings → Environment Variables
### Added
#### New Feature: 🏷️ Model Categories
- Tag any model in the **Checkpoint Manager** with as many custom categories as you like, e.g. *Character*, *Style* or *Concept*, shown as coloured chips on its card. The most requested item on our feature tracker
- Filter from the new **Categories** sidebar section or with `@name` in the search box, and assign in bulk from the selection bar, with right-click → **Set Categories**, or by dropping cards onto a category
- **Manage Categories** reorders categories by dragging and deletes them, and new categories pick their own colour from a palette of presets
- Categories reach **Inference** too: the model picker gets a **Categories** filter row and shows each model's chips, and typing a category name filters model dropdowns and the `<lora:` autocomplete
- Categories are stored in the model's `.cm-info.json`, so they survive moves, renames and metadata refreshes
#### New Feature: 📋 Inference Prompt Queue
- Queue up generations from any Inference tab with **Add to Queue** next to Generate, and run them one after another ([#1622](https://github.com/LykosAI/StabilityMatrix/issues/1622))
- Each item keeps the full project state, so **Open in tab** brings it back as a real tab to tweak and re-queue. Cards show live progress, a preview and the finished thumbnail
- Reorder, remove, cancel and re-queue items freely. **Start** connects to ComfyUI or offers to launch it, and **Pause** finishes the current item first
- The queue is saved to your library folder and survives restarts
#### New Feature: 🎬 MiniMax H3 Video in Inference
- Generate video **with native stereo audio** using **MiniMax H3** in the **Text to Video** and **Image to Video** tabs, up to about 15 seconds at 24 fps (needs ComfyUI 0.33 or newer)
- Pick an H3 model and the tab sets itself up: ✨ recommended settings, one-click downloads for the official text encoder and video/audio VAEs, and GGUF models work too. Set an **Audio VAE** to get the soundtrack in your mp4
- Videos generated in Inference now **play inside the app**, in the Inference gallery, the Outputs page and the image viewer. The preview is muted, and *Open in external player* gets you the audio. The outputs strip lists videos too
- The video model card spots a few-step **Lightning / turbo LoRA** running at a CFG above 1 and offers a one-click switch to matching settings
#### New Feature: 🎨 New Models in Inference
- **Qwen Image** (2512), **Krea 2 Turbo** (8-step) and **Krea 2 Raw** workflow profiles, with auto-detection, automatic text encoder and VAE pairing, and one-click recommended sampler settings. Qwen-tagged CivitAI checkpoints now go to the DiffusionModels folder
- **MOSS Image** (Base and SFT), with one-click downloads for its Qwen3.5 9B text encoder and the Flux.2 VAE
- **Wan 2.2 14B** mixture-of-experts video models: enable **Dual expert (high / low noise)** from the Wan model card's ⚙️ menu to run the two-pass sampling 14B expects, with a separate **Low-Noise LoRAs** list for per-expert speed LoRAs. Picking one half of a pair offers to load the other
- All of these need an up-to-date ComfyUI, so update your package if a workflow is rejected
#### New Feature: ⬇️ One-Click Text Encoder & VAE Downloads
- When your model needs a text encoder or VAE you don't have, the Model card says what's missing and offers the official download in one click, for Flux, Flux.2 (4B/9B-aware), Z-Image, Anima, HiDream, Qwen Image, Krea 2 and MOSS Image
- Only official shared components are offered, so any CivitAI fine-tune still works. Finished files select themselves
#### New Feature: 🤗 Live HuggingFace Model Browser
- The HuggingFace tab is now a full browser: search HuggingFace by downloads, likes or recent updates, or paste a repository link to browse all of its files. The curated picks are still the default view
- Browse files as a list or folder tree, pick each file's destination (auto-detected, including text encoders), or send a whole multi-file repository into one folder. See the total size before you start
- Gated or private repositories work once you add a HuggingFace token in **Settings → Accounts**
#### New Feature: 🧩 Persistent Inference Layouts
- Rearranged panes in Inference now stick, one of our most requested features ([#1340](https://github.com/LykosAI/StabilityMatrix/issues/1340)). Layouts are kept per tab type, **saving a project** stores its layout, and **Restore Default Layout** resets the current tab
- Added **IP-Adapter** to the Inference sampler's **Addons**: guide a generation with a reference image for style, composition or subject, with one-click downloads for the IP-Adapter and CLIP Vision models
- Added a **Skip Layer Guidance** addon to the Inference sampler. It starts on MOSS Image's recommended settings and also works with other DiT models like SD 3.5
- Added a **gallery picker** for the Inference **+** button, grouping project types into **Image / Video / Legacy**. Prefer the old dropdown? Turn on **Compact New Tab Menu** in Settings → Inference
- Added a **What's New** viewer under **Settings → About** to read the release notes for any version, with a one-time heads-up after each update
- The **Workflows** library groups workflows by folder, shows **Installed** / **Update Available** on Model Browser cards for imported workflows, and adds **Edit Metadata** and **Check Required Nodes** to workflow cards
- Added **uv cache** management under **Settings → Package Environment**: see the cache size, clear it with progress, and set an optional size limit ([feature request](https:

gpt4all.changelog:
## What's New
* **Remote Models:**
  * The Add Model page now has a dedicated tab for remote model providers.
  * Groq, OpenAI, and Mistral remote models are now easier to configure.
* **CUDA Compatibility:** GPUs with CUDA compute capability 5.0 such as the GTX 750 are now supported by the CUDA backend.
* **New Model:** The non-MoE Granite model is now supported.
* **Translation Updates:**
  * The Italian translation has been updated.
  * The Simplified Chinese translation has been significantly improved.
* **Better Chat Templates:** The default chat templates for OLMoE 7B 0924/0125 and Granite 3.1 3B/8B have been improved.
* **Whitespace Fixes:** DeepSeek-R1-based models now have better whitespace behavior in their output.
* **Crash Fixes:** Several issues that could potentially cause GPT4All to crash have been fixed.

koodo-reader.changelog:
## New Features

- Added OCR plugin functionality; go to Settings > Plugins
- Added support for the following file formats: caj, djvu, xps, chm, doc, rtf, pptx, ppt, ofd, djv, oxps, and ofd
- The reading page now supports an immersive title bar, which automatically hides while reading
- Reading options now support grouped display
- Added book collections and grouping features, allowing you to combine and manage multiple books together
- Support for adjusting page spacing in double-page view; go to Reading Options on the right > Layout
- Support for right-to-left page turning; go to Reading Options on the right > Layout
- Support for exporting book packages: Book files, along with notes, highlights, bookmarks, and dictionary history, are bundled into a single new file for easy sharing with others or importing onto new devices
- Added a prompt asking whether to clear all data upon uninstallation
- Support for parsing ISBN, publication date, modification date, language, and other information from book files
- Optimized for comics in EPUB, MOBI, and AZW3 formats, with support for double-page mode and continuous scrolling
- Added an auto-read feature that automatically scrolls pages at a specified speed; tap the “Assisted Reading” button in the top-right corner
- Added options to clear temporary cache and TTS cache; go to Settings > Data
- Added a pop-up prompt before opening external links
- Support for hiding the built-in background in text-only PDFs
- Support for clearing all keyboard shortcuts
- Optimized chapter division rules for TXT files
- (Mobile) Reading settings are divided into Basic Settings and Advanced Settings; Advanced Settings now support grouped display
- (Mobile) Added support for MEGA cloud storage
- (Mobile) Added an option to automatically adjust reading brightness
- (Mobile) The native PDF reader and comic reader now support page turning via volume keys
- (Mobile) Added Data Management to Settings, which displays cache and total data sizes
- (Mobile) Added support for adjusting the threshold for automatically clearing temporary cache; go to Settings > Data Management
- (Mobile) Added support for clearing the TTS cache; go to Settings > Data Management
- (Mobile) Added an overlay animation for page-turning
- (Mobile) Sorting by book title now supports sorting by numerical order
- (Mobile) Added support for djvu, xps, chm, doc, rtf, pptx, ppt, ofd, djv, oxps, and ofd file formats

readest.changelog:
## Release Highlights
* Vocabulary: You can now build a vocabulary list, mark words as Learning or Mastered for Word Lens hints, and sync with Anki
* Statistics: Added a reading statistics dashboard so you can see your reading habits at a glance
* Reading: Added Page Flip and paper curl page turns, a page preview while dragging the progress slider, a straight-line reading ruler, and keyboard-only text selection
* Styling: You can now ignore publisher fonts, make white image backgrounds transparent, and adjust dialogue highlighting
* Text-to-Speech: You can now preview voices, pick a default voice per language, and sync downloaded read-aloud audio across devices
* Library: You can now import pasted text and Word or RTF files, share collections as bundles, search for covers in the app
* Sync: Added Grimmory, Obsidian, and CrossPoint 2.0 highlight sync, a new view of where your reading data goes, and a switch for servers with self-signed certificates
* Dictionary: You can now resize the dictionary popup, customize AI context lookups, edit word hints, and choose your lookup app on Android
* PDF: Text is now sharper, especially on iOS and Android, with smoother pinch zoom, panning, and gapless horizontal scrolling
* More: The KOReader plugin can sign in with a QR code, iPhone Duo gets book mode on its inner display, and stylus annotation and sync are more reliable

appflowy.changelog:
### 🚀 v0.15.1

#### Improvements

- **Feed discussions** — Opened comment threads in a popover on the card, with replies and drafts retained when the popover was dismissed.
- **Database row actions** — Enabled row creation from List and Gallery group headers, added Copy link to Gallery cards in cloud and self-hosted workspaces, and kept peek navigation in grouped List order.
- **Database history** — Clarified that row counts covered the whole saved database and that row-page content had its own history. Kept preview tabs and names tied to the saved version, excluding linked views embedded elsewhere.

#### Bug Fixes

- Fixed missing Gallery groups, empty-group visibility, and loading additional cards within large groups. Corrected List property alignment and gaps around empty Gallery and Feed properties.
- Preserved pending text, number, and rollup filter values when closing their editors, and prevented blank checklist tasks.
- Corrected date-only formula comparisons to use calendar days, while retaining precise comparisons when either date included a time.
- Restored reciprocal relation links when duplicating database rows.
- Preserved embedded databases and linked views in row templates opened and edited across Web and Desktop.
- Restored Person names in database history, row properties, and group headers.
- Recovered page references from outdated access denials and kept copied subpages visible after duplication completed.
- Fixed restored tabs that stayed blank after another tab was closed, and corrected row highlights and navigation between peek surfaces.
- Prevented reopened database views from staying in a loading state after their rows had finished loading. Suspended repeated upload and restore checks for unavailable databases while retaining recovery data for a later retry.
- Fixed stuck image-upload progress and recovery when selecting the same file again. Prevented incomplete uploads from being marked successful, waited for comment attachments to finish uploading before publishing them, and reduced repeated downloads of missing images.
- Kept notification lists readable when a newer server returned an unfamiliar notification type, and prevented malformed document block data from hanging reads or producing incomplete exports.
- Fixed missing PDF preview libraries in Windows packages and Windows native-updater registration. Fixed Linux shortcut errors caused by delayed key events after unregistration.

The minimum self-hosted server version remained **AppFlowy Cloud v0.19.10**.

## What's Changed

**⚠️ This update contains important security fixes. Please upgrade as soon as possible**.

- Shared decks could execute arbitrary code via iframes when viewed in the editor ([GHSA-j9v5-m549-cg6c](https://github.com/ankitects/anki/security/advisories/GHSA-j9v5-m549-cg6c)). Thanks to @DePierre for the report.
- On macOS, shared decks could execute arbitrary commands via specially crafted image filenames when the "Show in Folder" editor action is used ([GHSA-gfvm-4968-jp9m](https://github.com/ankitects/anki/security/advisories/GHSA-gfvm-4968-jp9m)). Thanks to @hyperreality and @Hama1cco for the reports.
- Compromised eMudhra intermediate CA certificates are now disallowed. This is in response to a [widespread security incident](https://emudhra.we-have-a-problem.com/) affecting most systems and web browsers. **Updating Anki might not be enough. Please make sure your system is fully up to date.**

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ankitects/anki/compare/26.09.3...26.09.4

zettlr.changelog:
**Quality of Life Improvements | Cleanup | Fixes**

This new update of Zettlr primarily fixes things that were either broken for some time, or broke in 4.9. However, it also includes a set of features and other improvements that will come in handy.

Among the most notable changes in this update are: (1) attachments specified in BibTeX or BibLaTeX libraries are properly opened via the context menu in Zettlr; (2) Mermaid diagrams will render again; (3) keywords and tags in YAML frontmatters are clickable again; (4) we fixed a bunch of shortcuts that stopped working after the custom shortcut update; (5) the LanguageTool linter now additionally checks various text-fields in your frontmatters; and (6) we have begun homogenizing Zettlr's UI across all platforms. macOS-users should not see many differences, but on Windows and Linux, the app will look considerably different. This change does not affect the placement or functionality of any UI elements, only their styling.

There's much more that has changed, so we again invite you to read the Changelog below before updating. Happy writing!

> **Do you enjoy Zettlr? Then consider making a donation to help us pay for the development costs. You can donate [monthly on Patreon](https://www.patreon.com/zettlr) or [once via PayPal](https://www.paypal.me/hendrikerz). Additionally, you can directly [sponsor Hendrik Erz on GitHub](https://github.com/sponsors/nathanlesage) or [send a tip on Ko-Fi](https://ko-fi.com/hendrikerz). Thanks for your support!**

# Changelog

## GUI and Functionality

- **Feature**: The context menus for links and images now also feature various
  items that may be useful for formatting aspects of the link/image descriptions
  (#6417).
- **Feature**: Make the "find next" and "find previous" commands of the editor
  search configurable. Previously, both `Mod-g` and `F3` would move to the next
  search result, but after implementing custom shortcuts, these two commands
  were left unconfigurable and hard-coded to `Mod-g`. These are now configurable
  so that you can change the default keybinding of `Mod-g` to `F3` if you wish
  (#6575).
- **Feature**: The LanguageTool linter now also lints text-only properties in
  the frontmatter, using the same language as the rest of the document. This
  allows spotting issues with these metadata fields as well. Currently, the
  linter includes in its detection the following properties:
    - `title`
    - `subtitle`
    - `abstract`
    - `abstract-title`
    - `description`
    - `shorttitle`
    - `shortsubtitle`
    - `thanks`
- **Change**: The styles and layouts of various UI components have been
  adjusted. The following components should now look mostly the same across all
  operating systems:
    - Toolbar
    - File Tree
    - Sidebar
- **Change**: Removed the `.md` extension from the default new filename pattern
  in the Advanced Preferences menu. This pattern is used as the filename, so the
  extension is unnecessary. Previously, creating a new file with the default
  pattern would result in the `.md` extension being added twice to markdown
  files, or added incorrectly to non-markdown files. Existing users should
  update the pattern manually by removing `.md` from it. For new installations,
  the pattern will be correct. (#6638).
- **Change**: The layout of the document information popover is now improved.
  We have moved the bold styling over to the actually important parts, improved
  legibility of the popover, and included more information -- notably,
  regardless of which unit (words or characters) you select in the preferences,
  the popover will now display both numbers, with your preferred one clearly
  visible.
- Fixed a misaligned size distribution between the file manager, editor view,
  and sidebar. Now, when double-clicking the dividers between these three
  components, they will resize so that both sidebars take up 20% of the window
  width, as opposed to a distribution of 20% for the file manager and ca. 15%
  for the sidebar. This way, both sidebars of the main window are visually
  equally sized.
- Fixed a bug where Zettlr would *never* load attachments from your main
  database if that database was in `BibTeX` or `BibLaTeX` format, as a small
  logical error made the relevant code for retrieving attachments never find the
  database in memory and thus would always fall back to attempting to contact

[Code signing policy](https://github.com/subhra74/xdm/blob/master/CODE_SIGNING_POLICY.md)

## What's Changed

### Downloads
- Better handling of busy servers: a download keeps going while a server limits or refuses its extra connections, and waits as long as the server asks (`Retry-After`, up to 5 minutes). When every connection is waiting, the list and progress window show **"Server busy, retrying at …"**. After 5 minutes with no data it stops with "The server is busy. Try again later."
- HLS videos from sites whose playlist link works only once now download: XDM uses the playlist the browser already loaded instead of fetching it again.
- Fixed a CDN refusing every request (HTTP 410) because of the order and case of request headers.
- **"Start downloads immediately"** now covers captured videos too: they start with the video dialog's usual choices (category and folder rules, segment count, default subtitle, Save as SRT) instead of always showing the dialog (#1426).
- Changing the default download folder now offers to move category folders that sit inside the old one. Files already downloaded stay where they are.
- Refresh link: the window now shows the page address with a copy button, so you can open it in the browser that has the XDM extension.

### Linux
- New **Flatpak** bundle for x64 and ARM. Double-click it to install in GNOME Software or KDE Discover, or run `flatpak install --user <file>`. The first install also downloads the Flatpak runtime from Flathub; XDM updates still come from this page.
- "Keep the computer awake" now uses the desktop's sleep-inhibit portal on every Linux install, with `systemd-inhibit` as the fallback.
- "Shut down when downloads finish" also tries logind, so it works on more desktops.

### Windows
- Fixed **"Failed to launch JVM"** at startup when the Java Access Bridge (screen reader support) is enabled (#1456).
- Installer: clearer wording on the Windows Firewall page.

### Look and feel
- Brighter selection in the sidebar and Classic list in both themes, with subtitle and count colours that meet the 4.5:1 contrast ratio.
- Dark theme improvements, including white button text and a dimmer disabled button.

### Bundled Java runtime
- Windows and macOS: updated to Liberica JDK 25.0.5.1, which fixes CVE-2026-114938 (a JIT Base64 bug on x86-64 CPUs with AVX-512 VBMI). Linux keeps JBR 25.0.4.1 with the affected JIT code turned off until a fixed JBR is released.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/subhra74/xdm/compare/9.0.11...9.0.12

FreeCAD 1.1.4 is the last planned maintenance release in the 1.1.x series. Firefox の標準リリース周期は 2 週間に短縮され、Floorp もこれまで以上に頻繁に Firefox の変更に対応する必要があります。Floorp は Firefox をベースに多数の独自機能を提供しているため、Firefox 本体の変更と独自機能の組み合わせで予期しない不具合が起こることがあります。 [Mozilla のリリース周期に関する案内](https://blog.mozilla.org/sumo/2026/08/19/firefox-new-release-cadence-and-what-to-expect/)

**今後数か月間、Floorp は新機能の開発・追加を原則として一時停止し、既存機能の修正と安定性の向上に開発リソースを集中します。**

この期間は、以下の改善を優先します。

- 既知の不具合やクラッシュの修正
- Firefox の更新に伴う互換性問題への対応
- タブ、ワークスペース、サイドバーなどの既存機能の安定化
- 自動テストと回帰テストの強化
- 問題のある機能を安全に無効化できる仕組みの検討

セキュリティアップデートや必要な修正パッチは、この期間も引き続き提供します。

Floorp を毎日安心して使っていただけるよう、まずは既存の機能が確実に動作することを優先します。新機能を楽しみにしてくださっている皆さまにはお待ちいただくことになりますが、Floorp の開発は今後も続けていきます。引き続き、ご理解とご協力をよろしくお願いいたします。

Floorp Projects

## Floorp’s development priorities for the coming months

Thank you for using Floorp.

We’ve recently received several reports of bugs after Floorp updates and of conflicts affecting existing features. We’re grateful to everyone who has reported issues and helped us investigate them.

Firefox has moved to a standard two-week release cycle, so Floorp needs to adapt to Firefox changes more frequently. Floorp builds on Firefox with many features of its own, and changes in Firefox can interact with those features in unexpected ways. [Mozilla’s announcement about the Firefox release cycle](https://blog.mozilla.org/sumo/2026/08/19/firefox-new-release-cadence-and-what-to-expect/)

**For the next few months, we’ll generally pause development and rollout of new Floorp features and focus on fixing and improving the stability of existing features.**

During this period, we’ll prioritize the following work.

- Fixing known bugs and crashes
- Addressing compatibility issues introduced by Firefox updates
- Improving the stability of existing features such as tabs, workspaces, and the sidebar
- Strengthening automated tests and regression coverage
- Exploring ways to safely disable features that are causing problems

We’ll continue to provide security updates and necessary bug fixes throughout this period.

We want Floorp to be a browser you can rely on every day. If you’ve been looking forward to new features, thank you for your patience while we focus on making the features you already use work reliably. We’ll continue developing Floorp and appreciate your understanding and support.
